title: Discovery Module Contract
description: Contract for modules/discovery, implemented in 11_Benchmark_Engine/modules/discovery/. Discovery is the reconnaissance stage that runs before Vision: given only a URL, it understands an unknown travel website through safe, narrowly-scoped exploration (dismissing a cookie banner, expanding a collapsed nav menu) and read-only observation — never search, forms, login, booking, checkout, or any transaction. It produces a DiscoveryReport describing the site, then decides (rule-based, no AI calls) a suggested_benchmark_journey and a single safe_next_action for the orchestrator to hand to Vision. v0.2.0 renames several fields and adds consent_status/actions_taken/safe_next_action versus the v0.1.0 shape, reflecting the move from pure observation to bounded safe interaction.

WebsiteType.description: Matches the category vocabulary already rendered by 10_Dashboard/public/app.js's CATEGORY_CLASS badges, plus 'Other/Unknown' for a low-confidence guess.

SafeActionType.description: The only two interactions this module is ever allowed to perform.

DiscoveryInput.description: What the orchestrator hands Discovery. A URL is the only hard requirement — the platform's starting condition is 'given only a URL'.

company_slug.description: Optional hint, matching a Master_Benchmark_Matrix.json companies key if this is a known re-benchmark.

company_name.description: Optional hint, used only for display/logging.

DiscoveryOutput.description: The Discovery Report. Reflects one homepage visit plus at most two safe, reversible UI actions (see actions_taken) — never a second page, never a transaction.

resolved_url.description: The URL actually rendered after any redirect — comparing this to requested_url is itself an obstacle signal (login_wall, geo-redirect).

confidence.description: Overall confidence in this report as a whole.

navigation.description: Main navigation links as observed, after any safe menu-expand action.

primary_user_goals.description: What a user can plausibly accomplish here, inferred from which journey steps got applicable_guess=true, ordered by suggested_benchmark_journey's priority. Falls back to the meta description when nothing matched.

detected_ai_capabilities.description: Zero or more AI-related signals found, strongest evidence first.

visible_entry_points.description: Consolidated, de-duplicated doors into the product — nav links, CTAs, AI surfaces, search, account — for Vision to choose where to look next. Distinct from the raw navigation list.

consent_status.description: Reflects the outcome of the safe-exploration attempt, not just whether a banner exists. No vendor guess — vendor fingerprinting would require a hardcoded product-selector table, which this module deliberately avoids.

dismissed.description: True only if Discovery itself clicked an Accept-style control this run.

obstacles.description: Anything still standing in the way after safe exploration — informs whether Vision should escalate per the Tier 1/2/3 ladder.

suggested_benchmark_journey.description: One entry per canonical journey step, ordered by capture priority (AI interaction first when evidenced, per CLAUDE.md's AI-first mandate, then by confidence). Replaces vision.schema.json's VisionInput.journey_steps as a discovered, provisional list rather than an assumed one.

applicable_guess.description: Best-effort guess only — Vision's actual capture is what confirms or overturns this.

safe_next_action.description: The single rule-based recommendation for what the orchestrator should do next (proceed to Vision at a given step, retry, or escalate to hybrid research). Not free-form AI output — deterministic given the fields above.

actions_taken.description: Audit trail of every click Discovery actually performed this run. Empty when nothing needed clearing.

evidence.description: The accessible name of the control that was clicked.
